items.title: CVE-2026-133075
items.summary: A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to insufficient authorization checks in the quiz random question filter web service, an authenticated user with teacher privileges can modify random question settings in quizzes they do not have permission to manage. This flaw allows unauthorized users to alter assessment configurations across courses they do not oversee.

items.title: CVE-2026-133072
items.summary: A flaw was found in Moodle. Insufficient authorization checks in the quiz editing functionality allow an authenticated user with teacher privileges to view slot details and modify sections of quizzes they do not have permission to manage. An attacker could exploit this flaw to alter quiz configurations or disclose quiz structure information without proper authorization.

items.title: CVE-2026-133071
items.summary: A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to a missing authorization check when editing Lesson activity pages, authenticated users with teacher privileges can view and move lesson pages from courses they are not permitted to access into their own lessons. This issue can lead to unauthorized access and modification of restricted course content.

items.title: CVE-2026-133070
items.summary: A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to a missing authorization check when viewing and restoring wiki page versions, an authenticated user can access content from courses they are not permitted to view. This issue allows an attacker to inspect restricted course material and copy it into their own wiki pages, leading to unauthorized information disclosure.

items.title: CVE-2026-133069
items.summary: A flaw was found in Moodle. Missing authorization checks in the forum discussion web services allow authenticated users to view discussion information in courses they do not have permission to access. In addition, users with teacher privileges may lock forum discussions in courses where they lack proper authorization. This issue can lead to unauthorized information disclosure and unauthorized discussion state modification.

items.title: CVE-2026-133066
items.summary: A flaw was found in Moodle. Missing ownership verification in Feedback activity templates allows an authenticated teacher to view, use, or delete templates associated with courses other than their own. This can result in unauthorized access, modification, or deletion of course materials.

items.title: CVE-2026-133065
items.summary: A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to insufficient permission checks and input validation in the quiz question bank callback, an authenticated user can access and view questions from question banks they do not have permission to access. Furthermore, this issue allows users to trigger arbitrary class instantiation (creating unintended application objects), potentially leading to further unauthorized actions.

items.title: CVE-2026-133064
items.summary: A flaw was found in Moodle. Insufficient sanitization of objective identifiers in the SCORM (Sharable Content Object Reference Model) objectives report allows an authenticated user with content upload permissions to inject malicious scripts. When another user views the report, the injected script executes in their browser session, potentially allowing the attacker to access sensitive information or perform unauthorized actions on their behalf.

items.title: CVE-2026-133063
items.summary: A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to insufficient validation when saving activity settings, an authenticated user with teacher privileges can modify activities in courses they are not authorized to access. This flaw allows unauthorized changes to course materials, compromising the integrity of course content.

items.title: CVE-2026-133062
items.summary: A flaw was found in Moodle's external database enrolment plugin. Insufficient sanitization of data passed to queries against the external database allows an authenticated user with course editing permissions to perform a Structured Query Language (SQL) injection attack. When this non-default plugin is enabled, an attacker can exploit this issue to view, modify, or delete sensitive records within the connected external database.

items.title: CVE-2026-133061
items.summary: A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to a missing capability check in the grade items web service, an authenticated user with a student role can view the names of all grade items in a course, including those intended to be hidden. This flaw leads to unauthorized information disclosure of hidden course assessment details.

items.title: CVE-2026-62259
items.summary: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the experimental CRAM v4 functions cram_xpack_decode_char and cram_xrle_decode_char do not validate that attacker-controlled decode sizes remain within their expanded input arrays. Crafted CRAM data can therefore make either decoder read beyond the supplied input buffer, potentially disclosing process-state information or crashing the process through invalid memory access. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

Agents autonomously decompose tasks, execute subtasks and delegate remaining work to peers, enabling scalability and eliminating single points of failure. items.summary: arXiv:2611.25226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Provenance schemes such as those based on content watermarks let images from a generative model be traced back to it. items.title: Release-Bound Withdrawal Authorization for Bitcoin Custody
items.summary: arXiv:2611.25231v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A compromised cryptocurrency withdrawal backend can request signatures on unauthorized payments. Previously signed transactions may remain spendable after pause or become spendable again after a reorganization. Release-Bound Withdrawal Authorization (RBWA) orders permits against pause in a replicated journal and restores exposure when its closing evidence disappears from Bitcoin's active chain. items.summary: arXiv:2611.25272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The standard 5G Authentication and Key Agreement protocol (5G-AKA) authenticates subscriber credentials but does not verify the integrity of user equipment (UE). Existing literature includes admission-time device-certificate authentication and Trusted Platform Module (TPM)-based measured-boot attestation, which can additionally verify that the UE presents enrolled device credentials and boots into an approved state. items.summary: arXiv:2611.25301v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Split federated learning (SFL) distributes neural networks across clients and a server, coupling class-specific knowledge across their representations. items.title: LLM-Based Threat Detection and Prevention Framework for IoT Ecosystems
items.summary: arXiv:2505.00240v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The rapid expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) has introduced complex and evolving cybersecurity challenges. This paper presents a Large Language Model (LLM)-based framework for intelligent threat detection and prevention in IoT networks. items.title: Triosecuris: Formally Verified Protection Against Speculative Control-Flow Hijacking
items.summary: arXiv:2601.22978v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper introduces Triosecuris, a formally verified defense against Spectre BTB, RSB, and PHT that combines CET-style hardware-assisted control-flow integrity with compiler-inserted speculative load hardening (SLH). items.title: SST-Guard: Detecting and Characterizing Server-Side Google Analytics in the Wild
items.summary: arXiv:2604.27497v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As web browsers increasingly implement anti-tracking features, the web tracking ecosystem has been shifting from the client-side to the server-side. items.summary: arXiv:2606.28666v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Agent-based AI has enabled the automation of tasks by exposing application tools and resources to large language models (LLMs). items.summary: arXiv:2608.27496v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Tool-using LLM agents execute consequential operations on behalf of users. Because the LLM driving an agent processes trusted user instructions and untrusted content in the same context, agents are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection attacks that induce unintended actions by mixing malicious instructions into benign data. items.summary: arXiv:2610.07532v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: LLMs have advanced rapidly, raising growing concerns about their safety. Recent work has proposed approaches to detect and defend against attacks including defenses at decoding stage that leverage models' hidden states. However, existing decoding-stage defenses suffer from two limitations. First, they introduce a trade-off between safety and over-refusal, where strengthening safety degrades the model's helpfulness on benign queries. items.summary: arXiv:2610.16100v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A deniable authenticated key exchange (DAKE) establishes an authenticated shared key without giving third parties proof of participation. items.summary: arXiv:2611.12386v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the fingerprinting of agentic cyberattacks. Our objective is to reliably infer information about the attacker's configuration, such as LLM version and harness, from telemetry. items.title: Agent Meltdowns: The Road to Hell Is Paved with Helpful Agents
items.summary: arXiv:2605.19149v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Agents operating with computer and Web use inevitably encounter errors: inaccessible webpages, missing files, local and remote misconfigurations, etc. These errors do not thwart agents based on state-of-the-art models. items.title: QUASI: Post-Quantum Quorum Attestation of Pre-Validated Statements
items.summary: arXiv:2611.10403v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present QUASI, a newly conceived class of hash-based, post-quantum-secure protocols that enable a group of parties to produce a publicly verifiable attestation about a pre-validated statement.
